workflows.name: Organized Retail Crime (ORC) Investigation & Task Force

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitoring for resale of stolen BuildRight merchandise" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-create of "creates ORC case file" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify seal integrity, GPS tracking per W199" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: Organized Retail Crime (ORC) refers to professional theft rings that systematically steal from retail stores for resale, unlike opportunistic shoplifting handled by standard LP procedures (W466). For BuildRight with 200 stores and high-value merchandise (power tools, copper wire, appliances, branded hardware), ORC manifests as: (a) organized shoplifting rings hitting multiple stores in a region; (b) return fraud (stolen merchandise returned for cash/store credit using fake receipts); (c) employee-assisted theft (collusion between staff and external rings); (d) cargo theft during inter-island transit (W66); (e) vendor delivery short-shipment fraud. ORC is distinct from standard LP (W37, W466) in its scale, sophistication, and cross-store impact. W466 handles individual store-level LP incidents; this workflow handles the coordinated multi-store investigation and law enforcement engagement required for organized rings.
Controls: - CTL-306 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Audit Domains (PA-21.3).)
- operational: Loss Prevention Director review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cross-store evidence correlation difficulty**: With 200 stores using different CCTV systems (potentially different retention periods, different quality), correlating footage of the same individuals across stores in different cities is manually intensive and time-sensitive (30-day online retention per W71)

- **Employee collusion detection**: Internal LP systems (W466) are designed to detect individual employee theft; detecting coordinated collusion between employees at multiple stores requires advanced analytics and confidential investigation techniques that can be perceived as intrusive, creating HR and labor relations friction (W493)

- **Law enforcement capacity**: PNP CIDG has limited capacity for retail theft investigations; low-value individual cases (even if part of an organized ring) may not receive priority attention, reducing prosecution success

- **Social media resale detection**: Stolen BuildRight merchandise resold on Facebook Marketplace, Lazada, or Shopee is difficult to detect systematically; manual monitoring is labor-intensive and reactive

- **Jurisdictional complexity**: ORC rings operating across multiple cities and provinces involve multiple PNP jurisdictions; coordinating a multi-jurisdictional investigation requires significant law enforcement liaison effort
Staffing Implication: - **LP Director**: ~100–150 hours/year on ORC task force leadership. Absorbed within existing LP Director role.
- **LP Investigators**: ~200–400 hours/year on active investigations. Absorbed within existing LP team (dedicated to ORC as needed).
- **LP Analyst**: ~400–500 hours/year on pattern detection (part of existing EBR monitoring duties under W466).
- **No incremental headcount** — ORC is absorbed into existing LP function with reprioritization.
System Touchpoints: - Exception-Based Reporting (EBR) module (W466): pattern detection analytics
- POS Transaction Database: cross-store transaction correlation
- ORC Case Management System: case files, evidence tracking, law enforcement coordination
- Social Media Monitoring Tools: resale activity detection

- Integration with W37 (loss prevention), W466 (LPAP), W248 (inventory variance), W71 (CCTV), W92 (inventory adjustment), W140 (OHS — if employee injury during incident), W43 (separation — ORC-related termination)
Time Estimate: - Pattern detection and monitoring: ~8–10 hours/week (LP Analyst — absorbed from W466 duties)
- Active investigation: ~40–120 hours per case (LP Investigator)
- **Total annual**: ~400–600 hours for LP Director and LP Investigators

steps.activity: **Pattern Detection & Intelligence Gathering**: LP Analyst identifies ORC patterns from multiple data sources: (a) EBR exception reports (W466) — correlated voids, returns, and inventory shortages across multiple stores; (b) inventory shrinkage reports (W248) — stores with abnormal shrinkage spikes; (c) return transaction analysis — high-frequency returns across stores with similar merchandise, same customer IDs; (d) POS exception data — transactions involving same SKUs repeatedly at different stores; (e) external intelligence — industry ORC alerts from Philippine Retailers Association (PRA), local law enforcement bulletins; (f) social media monitoring for resale of stolen BuildRight merchandise (Facebook Marketplace, Lazada, Shopee)

**Case File Creation**: LP Director creates ORC case file: (a) case number, classification (organized shoplifting, return fraud, employee collusion, cargo theft, vendor fraud); (b) suspected ring profile (number of individuals, vehicles, stores targeted); (c) financial impact estimate (total known losses from correlated incidents); (d) scope: affected stores, regions, time period; (e) assign lead LP Investigator; (f) classify confidentiality level (ORC investigations are strictly confidential to avoid tipping off suspects)

**Cross-Store Investigation Coordination**: LP Investigator coordinates investigation across affected stores: (a) pull CCTV footage from all affected stores (W71) — look for common individuals, vehicles, methods; (b) correlate POS transaction data across stores — identify common payment methods, loyalty accounts, or patterns; (c) interview Store Managers and relevant staff confidentially; (d) cross-reference employee work schedules (W34) against incident times (for employee collusion cases); (e) coordinate with DC LP for cargo theft cases (verify seal integrity, GPS tracking per W199)

**Evidence Compilation**: LP Investigator compiles prosecution-ready evidence package: (a) chronological incident timeline across all affected stores; (b) CCTV footage compilation (edited highlights with timestamps); (c) POS transaction records (certified system extracts); (d) inventory shrinkage documentation (W248/W92); (e) employee statements (notarized if necessary); (f) financial impact quantification; (g) social media screenshots of suspected resale activity (with metadata preservation per Data Privacy Act W271)

**Law Enforcement Coordination**: LP Director coordinates with law enforcement for criminal prosecution: (a) for non-employee suspects: file complaint with PNP Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) or local PNP station; (b) for employee suspects: coordinate with VP Legal and HR for parallel criminal and administrative proceedings (DOLE due process per W43); (c) for cargo theft: coordinate with PNP Highway Patrol Group and port security; (d) provide evidence package to law enforcement; (e) assist in entrapment/buy-bust operations if requested by law enforcement; (f) attend court hearings as prosecution witness

**ORC Task Force Monthly Review**: LP Director chairs monthly ORC Task Force meeting: (a) review all active ORC cases and investigation status; (b) review new intelligence and pattern alerts; (c) assess financial impact of ORC losses vs. period; (d) coordinate with Regional Managers on store-level prevention measures; (e) review and update ORC prevention strategies (EAS tag placement, high-value item display security, return policy adjustments); (f) coordinate with IT on EBR rule enhancements (W466)

**Industry Coordination**: LP Director participates in industry ORC coordination: (a) attend quarterly Philippine Retailers Association (PRA) ORC working group meetings; (b) share non-confidential intelligence (modus operandi, known suspect profiles, vehicle descriptions) with peer retailers; (c) coordinate with competing hardware retailers on common ORC threats; (d) contribute to industry-wide ORC database (if available)

**Case Closure & Lessons Learned**: Upon case resolution: (a) LP Director prepares case closure report: total financial loss, recovery amount, criminal prosecution outcome, employees terminated, policy changes implemented; (b) conduct lessons learned session with affected stores; (c) update LP procedures and EBR rules (W466) to prevent recurrence; (d) update ORC intelligence database for future pattern recognition; (e) report outcome to VP Store Operations and CFO
